audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Joshua / Yehoshua Gibeonite treaty and forced-labor narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for coalition response, Gibeonite deception, moldy provisions, failure to inquire of YHWH, oath, public protest, survival, curse, and woodcutter/water-drawer status.

verses.restored: It was, when all kings who were across Jordan in hill country, in Shephelah, and along all coast of Great Sea toward Lebanon—Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite—heard,

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when all the kings which were on this side Jordan, in the hills, and in the valleys, and in all the coasts of the great sea over against Lebanon, the Hittite, and the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, heard thereof;

modern.text: Now when news of this reached all the kings west of the Jordan—those in the hill country, the foothills, and all along the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon (the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites)—

familiar.text: That they gathered themselves together, to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one accord.

modern.text: they came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.

modern.text: acted deceptively and set out as envoys, carrying on their donkeys worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended.

familiar.text: And old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy.

modern.text: They put worn, patched sandals on their feet and threadbare clothing on their bodies, and their whole supply of bread was dry and moldy.

original.text: וּנְעָל֨וֹת בָּל֤וֹת וּמְטֻלָּאוֹת֙ בְּרַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם וּשְׂלָמ֥וֹת בָּל֖וֹת עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְכֹל֙ לֶ֣חֶם צֵידָ֔ם יָבֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֥ה נִקֻּדִֽים

verses.restored: They went to Joshua at camp at Gilgal and said to him and men of Israel, From a far land we have come; now cut covenant with us.

familiar.text: And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us.

modern.text: They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant land; please make a treaty with us.”

original.text: וַיֵּלְכ֧וּ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו וְאֶל אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵאֶ֤רֶץ רְחוֹקָה֙ בָּ֔אנוּ וְעַתָּ֖ה כִּרְתוּ לָ֥נוּ בְרִֽית

verses.restored: Men of Israel said to Hivite, Perhaps you dwell in our midst; how then can we cut covenant with you?

familiar.text: And the men of Israel said unto the Hivites, Peradventure ye dwell among us; and how shall we make a league with you?

modern.text: But the men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you dwell near us. How can we make a treaty with you?”

original.text: ויאמרו אִֽישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל הַחִוִּ֑י אוּלַ֗י בְּקִרְבִּי֙ אַתָּ֣ה יוֹשֵׁ֔ב וְאֵ֖יךְ אכרות לְךָ֥ בְרִֽית

verses.restored: They said to Joshua, Your servants are we. Joshua said to them, Who are you, and from where do you come?

familiar.text: And they said unto Joshua, We are thy servants. And Joshua said unto them, Who are ye? and from whence come ye?

modern.text: “We are your servants,” they said to Joshua. Then Joshua asked them, “Who are you and where have you come from?”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֧ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ מִ֥י אַתֶּ֖ם וּמֵאַ֥יִן תָּבֹֽאוּ

modern.text: “Your servants have come from a very distant land,” they replied, “because of the fame of the LORD your God. For we have heard the reports about Him: all that He did in Egypt,

verses.restored: and all he did to two kings of Amorite beyond Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan who was at Ashtaroth.

familiar.text: And all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites, that were beyond Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon, and to Og king of Bashan, which was at Ashtaroth.

modern.text: and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan—Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth.

original.text: וְאֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה לִשְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן לְסִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן וּלְע֥וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּעַשְׁתָּרֽוֹת

verses.restored: Our elders and all inhabitants of our land spoke to us, saying, Take provisions in your hand for way and go to meet them and say to them, Your servants are we; now cut covenant with us.

familiar.text: Wherefore our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spake to us, saying, Take victuals with you for the journey, and go to meet them, and say unto them, We are your servants: therefore now make ye a league with us.

modern.text: So the elders and inhabitants of our land told us, ‘Take provisions for your journey; go to meet them and say to them: We are your servants. Please make a treaty with us.’

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלֵ֡ינוּ זְֽקֵינֵינוּ֩ וְכָל יֹשְׁבֵ֨י אַרְצֵ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר קְח֨וּ בְיֶדְכֶ֤ם צֵידָה֙ לַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וּלְכ֖וּ לִקְרָאתָ֑ם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֲלֵיהֶם֙ עַבְדֵיכֶ֣ם אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וְעַתָּ֖ה כִּרְתוּ לָ֥נוּ בְרִֽית

verses.restored: This our bread was hot when we took it for provisions from our houses on day we went out to come to you; and now, look, it is dry and crumbly.

familiar.text: This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and it is mouldy:

modern.text: This bread of ours was warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But take a look, it is now dry and moldy.

original.text: זֶ֣ה לַחְמֵ֗נוּ חָ֞ם הִצְטַיַּ֤דְנוּ אֹתוֹ֙ מִבָּ֣תֵּ֔ינוּ בְּי֥וֹם צֵאתֵ֖נוּ לָלֶ֣כֶת אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְעַתָּה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָבֵ֔שׁ וְהָיָ֖ה נִקֻּדִֽים

verses.restored: These wineskins were new when we filled them, and look, they are torn; and these garments and sandals became worn from very long way.

familiar.text: And these bottles of wine, which we filled, were new; and, behold, they be rent: and these our garments and our shoes are become old by reason of the very long journey.

modern.text: These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look, they are cracked. And these clothes and sandals are worn out from our very long journey.”

original.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה נֹאד֤וֹת הַיַּ֨יִן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִלֵּ֣אנוּ חֲדָשִׁ֔ים וְהִנֵּ֖ה הִתְבַּקָּ֑עוּ וְאֵ֤לֶּה שַׂלְמוֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּנְעָלֵ֔ינוּ בָּל֕וּ מֵרֹ֥ב הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: The men took from their provisions, but mouth of YHWH they did not ask.

familiar.text: And the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD.

modern.text: Then the men of Israel sampled their provisions, but did not seek the counsel of the LORD.

original.text: וַיִּקְח֥וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֖ים מִצֵּידָ֑ם וְאֶת פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א שָׁאָֽלוּ

verses.restored: Joshua made peace with them and cut covenant with them to let them live, and leaders of congregation swore to them.

familiar.text: And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them.

modern.text: And Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ לָהֶ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ שָׁל֔וֹם וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם בְּרִ֖ית לְחַיּוֹתָ֑ם וַיִּשָּׁבְע֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם נְשִׂיאֵ֖י הָעֵדָֽה

verses.restored: It was at end of three days after they cut covenant with them that they heard they were near to them and dwelt in their midst.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at the end of three days after they had made a league with them, that they heard that they were their neighbours, and that they dwelt among them.

modern.text: Three days after they had made the treaty with the Gibeonites, the Israelites learned that they were neighbors, living among them.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֕י אֲשֶׁר כָּרְת֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּרִ֑ית וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֗וּ כִּי קְרֹבִ֥ים הֵם֙ אֵלָ֔יו וּבְקִרְבּ֖וֹ הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel set out and came to their cities on third day: Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel journeyed, and came unto their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Gibeon, and Chephirah, and Beeroth, and Kirjathjearim.

modern.text: So the Israelites set out and on the third day arrived at their cities—Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ אֶל עָרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י וְעָרֵיהֶם֙ גִּבְע֣וֹן וְהַכְּפִירָ֔ה וּבְאֵר֖וֹת וְקִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel did not strike them because leaders of congregation had sworn to them by YHWH Divine of Israel; and all congregation murmured against leaders.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel smote them not, because the princes of the congregation had sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel. And all the congregation murmured against the princes.

modern.text: But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. And the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.

original.text: וְלֹ֤א הִכּוּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּֽי נִשְׁבְּע֤וּ לָהֶם֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הָֽעֵדָ֔ה בַּֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּלֹּ֥נוּ כָל הָעֵדָ֖ה עַל הַנְּשִׂיאִֽים

verses.restored: All leaders said to all congregation, We swore to them by YHWH Divine of Israel; now we may not touch them.

familiar.text: But all the princes said unto all the congregation, We have sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel: now therefore we may not touch them.

modern.text: All the leaders answered, “We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ כָל הַנְּשִׂיאִים֙ אֶל כָּל הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה אֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ נִשְׁבַּ֣עְנוּ לָהֶ֔ם בַּֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֕ה לֹ֥א נוּכַ֖ל לִנְגֹּ֥עַ בָּהֶֽם

verses.restored: This we will do to them and let them live, so wrath will not be against us because of oath we swore to them.

familiar.text: This we will do to them; we will even let them live, lest wrath be upon us, because of the oath which we sware unto them.

modern.text: This is how we will treat them: We will let them live, so that no wrath will fall on us because of the oath we swore to them.”

original.text: זֹ֛את נַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם וְהַחֲיֵ֣ה אוֹתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא יִֽהְיֶ֤ה עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ קֶ֔צֶף עַל הַשְּׁבוּעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּ֥עְנוּ לָהֶֽם

verses.restored: Leaders said to them, Let them live. So they became cutters of wood and drawers of water for all congregation, as leaders spoke concerning them.

familiar.text: And the princes said unto them, Let them live; but let them be hewers of wood and drawers of water unto all the congregation; as the princes had promised them.

modern.text: They continued, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation.” So the leaders kept their promise.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֧וּ אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם הַנְּשִׂיאִ֖ים יִֽחְי֑וּ וַ֠יִּֽהְיוּ חֹטְבֵ֨י עֵצִ֤ים וְשֹֽׁאֲבֵי מַ֨יִם֙ לְכָל הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבְּר֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם הַנְּשִׂיאִֽים

verses.restored: Joshua called them and spoke to them, saying, Why did you deceive us, saying, We are very far from you, when you dwell in our midst?

familiar.text: And Joshua called for them, and he spake unto them, saying, Wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you; when ye dwell among us?

modern.text: Then Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and said, “Why did you deceive us by telling us you live far away from us, when in fact you live among us?

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לָמָּה֩ רִמִּיתֶ֨ם אֹתָ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר רְחוֹקִ֨ים אֲנַ֤חְנוּ מִכֶּם֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְאַתֶּ֖ם בְּקִרְבֵּ֥נוּ יֹשְׁבִֽים

verses.restored: Now cursed are you; a servant shall not be cut off from you, cutters of wood and drawers of water for house of my Divine.

familiar.text: Now therefore ye are cursed, and there shall none of you be freed from being bondmen, and hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God.

modern.text: Now therefore you are under a curse and will perpetually serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה אֲרוּרִ֣ים אַתֶּ֑ם וְלֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֨ת מִכֶּ֜ם עֶ֗בֶד וְחֹטְבֵ֥י עֵצִ֛ים וְשֹֽׁאֲבֵי מַ֖יִם לְבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהָֽי

verses.restored: They answered Joshua and said, Because it was surely told to your servants that YHWH your Divine commanded Moses his servant to give you all land and destroy all inhabitants of land from before you; so we feared greatly for our souls/lives because of you and did this thing.

familiar.text: And they answered Joshua, and said, Because it was certainly told thy servants, how that the LORD thy God commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you, therefore we were sore afraid of our lives because of you, and have done this thing.

modern.text: The Gibeonites answered, “Your servants were told clearly that the LORD your God had commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land and wipe out all its inhabitants before you. So we greatly feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we have done this.

original.text: וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ כִּי֩ הֻגֵּ֨ד הֻגַּ֤ד לַעֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֜ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֔וֹ לָתֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אֶת כָּל הָאָ֔רֶץ וּלְהַשְׁמִ֛יד אֶת כָּל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֑ם וַנִּירָ֨א מְאֹ֤ד לְנַפְשֹׁתֵ֨ינוּ֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם וַֽנַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Now look, we are in your hand; as good and right in your eyes to do to us, do.

familiar.text: And now, behold, we are in thine hand: as it seemeth good and right unto thee to do unto us, do.

modern.text: Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה הִנְנ֣וּ בְיָדֶ֑ךָ כַּטּ֨וֹב וְכַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָ֖נוּ עֲשֵֽׂה

verses.restored: He did so to them and rescued them from hand of children of Israel, and they did not kill them.

familiar.text: And so did he unto them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, that they slew them not.

modern.text: So Joshua did this and delivered them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill the Gibeonites.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם כֵּ֑ן וַיַּצֵּ֥ל אוֹתָ֛ם מִיַּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְלֹ֥א הֲרָגֽוּם

verses.restored: Joshua made them on that day cutters of wood and drawers of water for congregation and for altar of YHWH, to this day, at place he would choose.

familiar.text: And Joshua made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation, and for the altar of the LORD, even unto this day, in the place which he should choose.

modern.text: On that day he made them woodcutters and water carriers, as they are to this day for the congregation of the LORD and for the altar at the place He would choose.

original.text: וַיִּתְּנֵ֨ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא חֹטְבֵ֥י עֵצִ֛ים וְשֹׁ֥אֲבֵי מַ֖יִם לָֽעֵדָ֑ה וּלְמִזְבַּ֤ח יְהוָה֙ עַד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחָֽר

translation_notes: The Gibeonites act under credible fear of extermination after hearing Jericho and Ai. Their deception is a survival strategy, not a trivial moral failure.
Verse 14 identifies Israel's procedural failure: the leaders inspect provisions but do not inquire of YHWH.
The oath is honored despite deception, preserving the principle that powerful parties remain bound by sworn protection.
The congregation protests the treaty, while leaders resist killing the protected population.
Woodcutter and water-drawer status preserves life but imposes hereditary forced labor and social subordination. Survival does not make the arrangement just.
The Gibeonites explicitly say they acted because they expected Israel to destroy all inhabitants, keeping conquest terror visible.
The text calls the arrangement a curse; modern reception must not romanticize coerced service as grateful inclusion or benevolent assimilation.
safety_note: Do not use Joshua 9 to justify slavery, caste, hereditary servitude, forced labor, exploitation of refugees, or punishment for deceptive survival under threat. Center the binding force of protection agreements, the duty to investigate before acting, preservation of life, and liberation beyond merely surviving as a subordinated labor class.
